explanation: Domain Bacteria contains the more common types of prokaryotes, with over 2,000 species named. Most bacteria are surrounded by a protective cell wall containing peptidoglycan. The Gram stain procedure is commonly used for diagnosing and classifying bacteria. Gram-positive bacteria retain the primary dye and appear purple after washing, while Gram-negative bacteria lose the dye and appear pink. Bacteria are also classified based on three physical shapes: spiral (spirilli), rod-shaped (bacilli), and round (cocci).

questions.q: What color do Gram-positive bacteria appear after the Gram stain washing step?
questions.exp: The notes state that 'Gram-positive bacteria retain dye and appear purple'.

questions.q: What are the three basic shapes used to classify bacteria?
questions.exp: The basic shapes and names listed are: Spiral (spirilli), Rod (bacilli), and Round (cocci).
